explain: _īdem_ is _is_ plus _-dem_: “the same”. For a masculine subject: _īdem vir_.
distractors: _eadem_ is feminine (“the same girl”). _vir_ is masculine: _īdem_.
_eundem_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _īdem_.
_eiusdem_ is genitive (“of the same”). A subject needs the nominative: _īdem_.
_eandem_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _eadem_.
_eundem_ is masculine accusative. A feminine subject needs _eadem_.

explain: Before _-dem_, _-m_ becomes _-n_: _eum + dem_ gives _eundem_. The same man as the thing seen: accusative.
distractors: _īdem_ is nominative. The thing seen is accusative: _eundem_.
_eōdem_ is ablative. The thing seen is accusative: _eundem_.

explain: For “the same thing” the neuter _idem_ stands alone as the object of _dīcō_.
distractors: _eundem_ is masculine accusative (“the same man”). “The same thing” is neuter: _idem_.
_eandem_ is feminine accusative. “The same thing” is neuter: _idem_.
_eiusdem_ is genitive (“of the same”). The thing said is accusative: _idem_.

en: We live in the same city.
explain: “In” (place) takes the ablative. _urbe_ is ablative feminine, so “the same” is _eādem_.
distractors: _eōdem_ is ablative masculine or neuter. _urbe_ is feminine: _eādem_.

explain: _eaedem_ is the feminine plural: _ea + dem_ with an _-ae_ ending, like _puellae_.
distractors: _eadem_ is singular (“the same girl”). _puellae_ is plural: _eaedem_.
_eōsdem_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _eaedem_.

explain: _ipse_ stresses a noun: “the man himself”, “in person”. It agrees with the noun in case, number and gender.
distractors: _ipsum_ is accusative (or neuter). A masculine subject needs _ipse_.
_ipsī_ is plural or dative. One man as the subject: _ipse_.
_ipsum_ is masculine accusative or neuter. A feminine subject needs _ipsa_.
_ipsam_ is accusative. A subject needs the nominative: _ipsa_.

explain: _ipsum_ agrees with _virum_ (accusative masculine): “the man himself” as the thing seen.
distractors: _ipse_ is nominative. The thing seen is accusative: _ipsum_.
_ipsī_ is dative or plural. The thing seen is accusative singular: _ipsum_.

explain: _ipsī_ is masculine plural nominative, agreeing with _virī_.
distractors: _ipsōs_ is accusative plural. A subject needs the nominative: _ipsī_.
_ipsīs_ is dative or ablative plural. A subject needs the nominative: _ipsī_.

en: I give a book to the master himself.
explain: The master receives the book, so _dominō_ is dative and the pronoun agrees: _ipsī_.
distractors: _ipsum_ is accusative. The one receiving is dative: _ipsī_.
_ipsō_ is ablative. The one receiving is dative: _ipsī_.
_ipse_ is nominative. The one receiving is dative: _ipsī_.
